verdict.rationale: Bento documents user-defined automations that run unattended in the background. You can describe failure modes in plain English, and Bento trains signals that fire in real time and backfill history (bentolabs-docs-4, bentolabs-docs-38). Natural-language alert rules compile to trace queries, route to Slack, PagerDuty, email or webhook, and incidents are automatically judged real or benign (bentolabs-docs-7, bentolabs-docs-45). Trigger-based fixes and nudges run in shadow mode and graduate to full traffic autonomously (bentolabs-docs-11, bentolabs-docs-12). These automations are limited to monitoring, alerting and fix promotion, not general-purpose workflows. Missing for 10: a general automation builder with arbitrary actions or schedules, detail on how users configure and control autonomous fix promotion, and independent or hands-on corroboration that these background automations work as claimed.
